P-8A Poseidon fires Harpoon | Royal New Zealand Air Force

In coordination with the Royal Australian Air Force and United States Navy, a Royal New Zealand Air Force P-8A Poseidon aircraft and crew from No. 5 Squadron successfully fired two AGM-84 Harpoon guided missiles at a decommissioned target ship, with both missiles hitting the target.
 
It was part of multi-domain Exercise Valiant Shield involving aircraft, ships and submarines from New Zealand, Australia, Canada, Japan and the United States.
 
“These activities are critical to the New Zealand Defence Force’s readiness to be able to meet the challenges of a deteriorating strategic environment, and we are incredibly grateful for the support of partners to assist us in regenerating the ability to rapidly strike targets at distance.” ~ Air Component Commander, Air Commodore Andy Scott

Full story ➡️ nzdf.mil.nz/P-8A-fires-Harpoon

Operating Theatres to Island Paradises: GynoMum's Life at Health NZ

What does work-life balance actually look like for a doctor? At Health New Zealand | Te Whatu Ora, we believe that a fulfilling medical career should go hand-in-hand with an extraordinary lifestyle.

In this video, GynoMum Michelle shares how relocating to Aotearoa New Zealand opened up a world of adventure, natural beauty, and adult discovery that they never dreamed possible while practising medicine elsewhere.

Learn more about what being an Obstetrician and Gynaecologist with Health New Zealand is like on our website ➡️ healthnz.govt.nz/OG

People ask me all the time why I moved to New Zealand – GynoMum shares the answer!

At Health New Zealand | Te Whatu Ora, we are incredibly proud of the collaborative, world-class environments we cultivate for our kaimahi (staff). 

In this video, GynoMum – a former New York City specialist – shares a firsthand look at why international medical professionals choose to build their careers and lives here in Aotearoa New Zealand.

From cutting-edge clinical resources to a deeply embedded cultural philosophy, we strive to build a health system that cares for our communities by first caring for our clinicians.

Learn more about what being an Obstetrician and Gynaecologist with Health New Zealand is like on our website ➡️ healthnz.govt.nz/OG

Offer more than just treatment – join us as a Radiation Therapist in New Zealand

In New Zealand, Radiation Therapists walk alongside their patients from the initial appointment through to the final treatment. This rare international scope of practice offers a rewarding career where the care you deliver truly matters.

The autonomy to practise across the full scope. And a life worth living outside of it.

Visit our website to find out more: http://healthnz.govt.nz/RT

The Big Drop-off

What can actually be recycled, and what still ends up in landfill?

In this episode, we join Kate from Wast-ed with Kate to explore our local transfer station and learn how small actions can make a big difference in reducing waste. We discover what items can be recycled for free, including paint tins, tyres, and other materials that don't need to end up in landfill.

Along the way, we uncover practical tips to help households reduce waste, recycle smarter, and make the most of the services available in our community.
 
Join us as we learn how easy it can be to divert waste from landfill and give everyday items a second life.

From Scraps to Snacks

What happens to our food scraps once they leave the kitchen? And how much work goes into growing the food we eat?

In this episode, we catch up with Kate from Wast-ed with Kate to learn how everyday food scraps can be transformed into tasty snacks instead of ending up in landfill. Kate shares practical tips for reducing food waste and making the most of what's already in our kitchens.

We also take a trip to a local potato farm to see firsthand the hard work, time, and care that goes into growing the produce we enjoy every day.
Join us as we explore simple ways to reduce waste, appreciate our food, and make more sustainable choices.

Like, subscribe, and share to help spread the word about reducing food waste.

Diving at RIMPAC | Royal New Zealand Navy

Maritime Explosive Ordinance Disposal (EOD) divers from HMNZS Matataua, the Royal New Zealand Navy's littoral warfare unit, are in Hawaii for Exercise RIMPAC.

The Officer in Charge explains what type of tasks the team will be conducting at the world's largest international maritime warfare exercise. A great opportunity to work with partners and share training insights and the latest operational techniques.

M2 .50-calibre machine gun | Royal New Zealand Navy

Packing a punch since 1918 💪 It is believed HMNZS Waikato was the first Royal New Zealand Navy vessel to be equipped with the M2 .50-calibre machine gun in 1966 but now the weapon, along with MARS L rifles, Glock pistols and Benelli shotguns are stock-standard small arms on our ships.
 
Designed by John Browning in 1918, the M2 .50 cal has been used by militaries around the world since 1933 in a number of variants.
 
The AN (Army Navy) version has a rate of fire between 750-850 rounds per minute at an effective range of 1,800 metres.

Aboard ships, its ease of use, robust design and reliability make it a vital force protection weapon and security deterrent, effective against surface and air targets.

POV: Combat Engineer | New Zealand Army

Clearing obstacles and creating opportunities 🛠️ Combat Engineers are the problem-solvers of the New Zealand Army.
 
They enable soldiers to move and operate by clearing routes and obstacles, handling explosives, constructing bridges, establishing water supplies, and building field defences.
 
Where others see obstacles, Combat Engineers see solutions.

Antarctic haven: protecting a global sanctuary

❄️🌊 Did you know the world’s largest marine protected area spans 1.55 million km²?
It’s in the Ross Sea, far south of Aotearoa New Zealand. New Zealand scientists and partners are monitoring the region to better understand climate impacts and ecosystem change. Science and international partnership are helping protect this global sanctuary!

It explores how New Zealand blends natural strengths with a progressive, partnership‑focused approach to business, and features insights from business leaders in New Zealand and around the world.

Hear why global partners choose to work with New Zealand, and how our way of doing business continues to create long‑term value across international markets.

Diving at RIMPAC | Royal New Zealand Navy

Maritime Explosive Ordinance Disposal (EOD) divers from HMNZS Matataua, the Royal New Zealand Navy's littoral warfare unit, are in Hawaii for Exercise RIMPAC.

The Officer in Charge explains what type of tasks the team will be conducting at the world's largest international maritime warfare exercise. A great opportunity to work with partners and share training insights and the latest operational techniques.

M2 .50-calibre machine gun | Royal New Zealand Navy

Packing a punch since 1918 💪 It is believed HMNZS Waikato was the first Royal New Zealand Navy vessel to be equipped with the M2 .50-calibre machine gun in 1966 but now the weapon, along with MARS L rifles, Glock pistols and Benelli shotguns are stock-standard small arms on our ships.
 
Designed by John Browning in 1918, the M2 .50 cal has been used by militaries around the world since 1933 in a number of variants.
 
The AN (Army Navy) version has a rate of fire between 750-850 rounds per minute at an effective range of 1,800 metres.

Aboard ships, its ease of use, robust design and reliability make it a vital force protection weapon and security deterrent, effective against surface and air targets.

POV: Combat Engineer | New Zealand Army

Clearing obstacles and creating opportunities 🛠️ Combat Engineers are the problem-solvers of the New Zealand Army.
 
They enable soldiers to move and operate by clearing routes and obstacles, handling explosives, constructing bridges, establishing water supplies, and building field defences.
 
Where others see obstacles, Combat Engineers see solutions.

P-8A Poseidon fires Harpoon | Royal New Zealand Air Force

In coordination with the Royal Australian Air Force and United States Navy, a Royal New Zealand Air Force P-8A Poseidon aircraft and crew from No. 5 Squadron successfully fired two AGM-84 Harpoon guided missiles at a decommissioned target ship, with both missiles hitting the target.
 
It was part of multi-domain Exercise Valiant Shield involving aircraft, ships and submarines from New Zealand, Australia, Canada, Japan and the United States.
 
“These activities are critical to the New Zealand Defence Force’s readiness to be able to meet the challenges of a deteriorating strategic environment, and we are incredibly grateful for the support of partners to assist us in regenerating the ability to rapidly strike targets at distance.” ~ Air Component Commander, Air Commodore Andy Scott

ASB Good as Gold: John Shepherd

This weeks’ ASB Good as Gold recipient is John Shepherd, founder of the ‘Every Sunday Collective’, a community he started eight years ago to support men’s mental health. What began with just five riders has grown into a welcoming network of more than 250 people who come together each Sunday to connect, talk, and ride. The Collective offers a space outside of everyday life where people can share stories, build friendships, and support one another. Under John’s guidance, the movement has expanded to South Auckland and Taupō, with Tauranga, Melbourne, and Sydney in the pipeline. John also plays a key role in leading ‘Every Sunday’ riders to take part in the annual Distinguished Gentleman’s Ride, helping raise funds and awareness for men’s mental health. His kōrero around positive mental health, inclusivity, and respect is both grounding and inspiring. Even while navigating personal challenges and caring for his family, John continues to lead with humility, compassion, and dedication. ASB is proud to recognise John Shepherd with $10,000 as this week’s ASB Good as Gold recipient.

Local Government Reform Meeting - 1 July 2026

The future of local government is being shaped right now — and this is our chance to help decide what it looks like for Waitaki.
As the Government’s Simplifying Local Government reforms get underway, we have a rare opportunity to shape representation in a way that is sustainable, affordable, and fit for future generations. 

But to make sure Waitaki’s voice is strong and well-informed, we need to hear from you. 

Your views will help ensure every perspective is considered as we prepare our submission.

These will begin with a panel discussion with the Mayor, the Chief Executive, and community representatives; Otto Dogterom and Justin Tipa, followed by a Q and A.
